newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil' real drops 0.03 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil' real drops 0.03 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.03 percent to close at 1.0810 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market in calm trading after the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.

The Central Bank depreciated the mini-band Thursday for the fourth time this month, lowering it 0.09 percent to between 1.0810 and 1.0860 reais per dollar through a buy/sell auction. The previous mini-band was set on July 11 at between 1.0800 and 1.0850 per greenback.
Dealers said Thursday's auction was absolutely routine and had been widely expected.
"The Central Bank just reaffirmed that its forex policy remains unchanged," one trader for a local investment bank said, referring to the routine lowering of the mini-band.

So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.42 percent against the dollar compared with monthly declines of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past six months. The Central Bank devalues the mini-band about five or six times a month.
Over the last few days, Brazilian spot forex markets remained calm despite the strong volatility in stock and futures markets, dealers said.
In late afternoon, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0810 per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market, dealers said.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.06 percent to close at 1.0873 per dollar.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.26 percent to end at 1.140 per dollar.
